title: Wren and the Safehouse
premise: Jude Pemberton, a financial-crimes investigator who launders his conscience alongside other people's money, has spent six years maintaining a safehouse for a handler he's never met — until the property appears on a real-estate site with interior photos that include his go-bag on the bed. The listing is bait, and the defector it's meant to flush out, a Russian accountant named Vera Sokolova, arrives at his door hours later, insisting she is the only one who can prove the summit's security apparatus has been sold. Jude must choose between his duty to hand her over and his growing conviction that the people he works for are the ones selling her — and the summit — to the highest bidder. In the end, Jude burns his own clean-money identity, exposes the leak using the very ledgers he built to hide, and escapes with Vera, alive but unmade, as the summit convenes without them.
about_author: Jude Galloway is the pen name of a former compliance analyst who spent a decade tracing money through shell companies before turning to fiction. They write thrillers about people who discover that the systems they serve were never on their side.

chapters.title: Clean Money
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A routine audit of a charity's accounts reveals a pattern Jude himself helped design — his own laundering architecture, repurposed. He goes home, checks the go-bag under the bed of his safehouse, and tells himself everything is fine. Beat: the polished lie beginning to crack.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A colleague sends him a real-estate link as a joke — the safehouse, for sale, with twelve interior photos. The thirteenth photo, deleted but cached, shows his go-bag. Jude realizes someone inside the network is selling him out. Beat: cold dread replacing routine.

chapters.title: Handler's Voice
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. His handler, known only as Corliss, orders him to stay put and prepare to receive an asset. The instructions contradict the listing's timeline. Jude begins keeping a private record — the first ledger of his own betrayal. Beat: suspicion turning inward.

chapters.title: The Woman at the Door
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Vera Sokolova arrives three days early, wet from the rain, carrying nothing but a burner phone and a name Jude recognizes from a frozen account. She says the summit's security contract was bought. He doesn't believe her — yet. Beat: wary, electric first contact.

chapters.title: Vera
chapters.summary: Vera's POV. Flashback to Moscow: the accounting firm, the ledger she copied, her brother's arrest used as leverage. She explains why she ran toward the safehouse instead of away from it — the listing was the only address she trusted to be compromised in the right way. Beat: her competence and desperation established.

chapters.title: Two Ledgers
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. He cross-checks Vera's claims against his own records and finds the summit's security vendor routes through the same shell network as his charity audit. Someone is monetizing both sides. He should report her. He doesn't. Beat: love against duty, first stirring.

chapters.title: Corliss Calls
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Corliss orders him to deliver Vera to a 'secondary site' — an address Jude's own architecture says doesn't exist. Vera, listening from the stairs, tells him that address is a grave. Beat: the handler's mask slipping; trust shifting to the defector.

chapters.title: The Neighbor
chapters.summary: Vera's POV. A neighbor photographs Vera through the window and posts it online. Within an hour, a car with diplomatic plates idles outside. Vera realizes the listing wasn't bait for her — it was bait for whoever came to collect her. Beat: the trap tightening around them both.

chapters.title: Go
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Night exfiltration through the back of the property, using a route Jude built for someone he assumed would be himself. They leave the go-bag behind as a decoy. Beat: the price of survival made physical — he burns his own contingency to save her.

chapters.title: Safehouse Two
chapters.summary: Vera's POV. A rented cottage by a freight line. Vera decodes her ledger while Jude watches the road, and they talk for the first time as people instead of assets. She asks what his real name is. He realizes he isn't sure anymore. Beat: identity as theme surfaces.

chapters.title: The Vendor
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude traces the security vendor to a holding company whose beneficial owner is a name from Corliss's own contact list. The summit isn't the target — it's the merchandise. Beat: rising stakes, the conspiracy takes shape.

chapters.title: Dead Drop
chapters.summary: Vera's POV. Vera insists on a meet with her old courier to verify a page of the ledger. Jude argues against it; she goes anyway. The courier arrives frightened, followed, and passes her a note: 'Your brother is alive. Cooperate.' Beat: hope weaponized against her.

chapters.title: What Vera Wants
chapters.summary: Vera's POV. Vera admits the enemy has her brother and that part of her came back to trade herself for him. Jude, furious, tells her she's the only proof that matters. They fight, then hold on to each other. Beat: the love declared in the middle of the lie.

chapters.title: The Auction
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude infiltrates a virtual data room where fragments of the summit's security plan are being shopped to three buyers. He recognizes the auctioneer's phrasing — it's Corliss's. Beat: betrayal confirmed; the personal becomes institutional.

chapters.title: Corliss
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude confronts Corliss at a marina. Corliss offers him a way out: walk away, keep the money, let the summit burn. Corliss claims Vera's ledger is forged and her brother is already dead. Beat: the offer Jude must refuse to remain himself.

chapters.title: Bait
chapters.summary: Vera's POV. Vera decodes the final page: the auction's centerpiece is a backdoor into summit security that only works if she's captured alive and made to 'confess.' She is the bait — and the product. Beat: her worst fear articulated, her resolve forged.

chapters.title: The Trade
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The enemy contacts Jude directly: Vera for her brother, at a freight yard, before the summit's first session. Jude agrees, planning the double-cross, knowing they'll plan one too. Beat: the gambit set; dread and determination in equal measure.

chapters.title: Freight Yard
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The exchange goes wrong on cue — but Jude has seeded the yard with the one thing he knows how to hide: money trails. He triggers the buyers' own compliance alarms, freezing the transaction mid-handoff. Beat: his shameful expertise becomes the weapon.

chapters.title: The Brother
chapters.summary: Vera's POV. In the chaos, Vera reaches her brother — and finds he was released weeks ago, a carrot kept in reserve, never a real hostage. The enemy's leverage was a story. She walks out of the yard on her own legs. Beat: the last chain cut; identity reclaimed.

chapters.title: Summit Morning
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude sends the full ledger — his own architecture, Corliss's auction, the vendor's backdoor — to three summit delegations simultaneously, making suppression impossible. Corliss is arrested at the perimeter. Beat: climax resolved by exposure, not violence.

chapters.title: Unmade
chapters.summary: Vera's POV. Aftermath: Jude's identity is burned, his accounts frozen, his name in the wind. Vera, granted no hero's welcome, chooses not to testify and disappear quietly. They meet once more, by a freight line, and decide to be no one together. Beat: the price of survival, paid and accepted.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, final chapter. Months later, a small rented flat, a new name — Wren, Vera's joke, a bird too plain to hunt. Jude unpacks a bag for the first time in six years and leaves it empty. Beat: quiet resolution; love chosen over duty, identity rebuilt from scratch.
